title: Are these pairs of creases on the folded sheet parallel?
description: A square sheet is folded in the middle, the edges are folded to the centre line, and two opposite corners are folded onto a crease to make triangles. The board checks each marked pair of creases for parallel lines. Keeko doubts that creases in different places can be parallel.
teaching_notes: One idea: parallel lines run the same way, and they are always in different places. Watch for students who think creases in different places cannot be parallel.

source: A square sheet is folded in the middle, the edges are folded to the centre line, and then two opposite corners are folded onto a centre crease to make triangles. Pairs of creases a and p, b and q, c and r are marked. Are they parallel?
video_script.why: The child checks pairs of creases on a folded sheet and gives a reason for each.
video_script.substitution: The book's own paper folding activity: the square sheet is folded in the middle and opened, the edges are folded to the centre line and opened, and two opposite corners are folded onto the creased line to make triangles.
video_script.anchor: A square sheet opened after its folds, with the creases a, b and c on one side and p, q and r on the other.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks creases in different places cannot be parallel.
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, eigh is parallel to p, b is parallel to q, and c is parallel to r.

final_answer.value: Yes: a is parallel to p, b to q and c to r
final_answer.spoken: yes, eigh is parallel to p, b is parallel to q, and c is parallel to r

hold_back: Yes: a is parallel to p, b to q and c to r
maths_rules: a and p lie along folds that run the same way, so they lie on parallel lines
b and q are both at right angles to those lines, so b and q are parallel to each other
c and r are the slanting edges of the two folded triangles, and both triangles are folded the same way, so c and r are parallel
the slip: parallel lines are always in different places, and what matters is the way they run
video_script.design: The opened sheet stays on the stage with its creases. Each pair lights up in its own colour as the board checks it.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book about a square sheet folded in several ways.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>First it is folded in the middle and opened. Then the edges are folded to the centre line and opened.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Then two opposite corners are folded onto the creased line to make triangles.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Are eigh, b and c parallel to p, q and r in that order? Say why or why not.
